From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

Below is my critical review of the Seller's draft from the Buyer's (Wattlebridge's) perspective. I've worked through each material issue, explained why it cuts against us, and set out where to push back. Recommendations are summarised at the end.

## A. Liability architecture — the cap/basket/time-limit package

**1. General cap at 20% / AUD 4.8m (Cl 12.1).** This is within market range for general warranties on a deal this size, but it is a negotiation anchor, not a given. 20% is at the lower end. Push for 25–30% (or higher) given the concentration risk in this business (see Bluefen below). More importantly, the cap only works if it is *paired* with proper carve-outs — which the Seller has deliberately collapsed (see point 3).

**2. Thresholds (Cl 12.2).** De minimis AUD 25,000 and basket AUD 250,000 are defensible in principle. Two things to check:
- Confirm the basket is a genuine **deductible/excess** (Seller says "only the excess above the basket is recoverable"). That is the Seller-favourable "excess only" form. We should push for a **tipping basket** (once you cross AUD 250k you recover from dollar one), or at least treat this as a trade against other points.
- The basket at ~1% of price is acceptable, but ensure de minimis items can aggregate toward the basket.

**3. "One limitation fits all Claims" (Cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5) — this is the most dangerous drafting move.** The Seller proposes that *every* limitation, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance and time bar "applies to all Claims of any nature" **unless expressly stated otherwise**. This is a trap: it silently sweeps **fundamental warranties, title, capacity, tax and the indemnities** into the same low cap and short time limits. **Reject the default.** The burden must be reversed — limitations apply *only* to general warranty claims unless expressly extended.

**4. Fundamental/Title warranties subjected to general cap and 18-month limit (expressly proposed).** Unacceptable. For "administrative simplicity" the Seller wants title and capacity — the very things that determine whether we actually acquire the company — capped at AUD 4.8m and time-barred at 18 months.
- **Title/capacity/ownership of shares** should be **uncapped (100% of price)** or near-100%, with a time limit of **6–7 years** (or no limit).
- This is especially important because **title is "evidenced" only by the Company's own share register (DD-012)** — see point K. We are taking title largely on trust, so the title warranty must have real teeth.

**5. Tax warranties/indemnity under the "general regime" (18 months).** Reject. Tax must track the statutory amendment period — a **tax deed/indemnity surviving ~7 years** (ATO amendment periods run up to 4 years, longer for fraud/evasion). An 18-month tax bar leaves us exposed to assessments that arise years later. The payroll tax/super/on-costs uncertainty on the DD-005 bonuses (point F) is a live tax exposure.

**6. General warranty time limit — 18 months.** Light. Push for at least **24 months** so we get through two full audit cycles. This is a reasonable ask and a good trade chip.

## B. Buyer knowledge / data-room constructive knowledge (Cl 8.3) + General disclosure (Schedule 7, Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2])

This is the second major structural problem, and it compounds the liability caps.

- **Cl 8.3** bars any claim for matters the Buyer *or its advisers* "had knowledge" of, **including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records."**
- The **Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]** then "discloses every fact... contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room" plus the Accounts, registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."

Together these create **sweeping constructive/deemed disclosure**: the Seller dumps the entire data room and claims it qualifies *all* warranties, while Cl 8.3 blocks claims on anything "discoverable." The effect is that the warranties are gutted — the very issues flagged in the Disclosure Letter (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the privacy incident) become disclosed and therefore non-claimable.

**Push back hard:**
- **Delete constructive/"discoverable" knowledge.** Limit any knowledge qualifier to the **actual knowledge** of a small, named deal team, and ideally delete it entirely (actual knowledge should not normally bar a bargained-for warranty).
- **Reject general/"sweeping" disclosure.** Disclosure should be **fair, specific and sufficiently detailed** to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. A warranty should only be qualified by matters **fairly disclosed** against the specific warranty, not by "everything referred to in the data room."
- Note [1.4]: the Seller reserves that nothing "admits... that any consent, payment, notice... is legally required." That's standard reservation language, but it signals the Seller is disclosing facts while denying they matter — all the more reason we need robust specific warranties and indemnities, not reliance on disclosure.

## C. Bluefen change-of-control consent (Cl 3/6.3; Disclosure §2) — CONDITION, not a warranty wrinkle

This is commercially the biggest single risk. Bluefen is **~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue** with a change-of-control clause (11.2) and conditions (11.3). The Disclosure confirms **no final written consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied.**

- Seller offers only "**reasonable endeavours**" and wants the condition deemed satisfied "**on delivery of the counterparty's written consent**." But it does not commit to *obtaining* consent, and the "deemed satisfied on delivery" language is circular — it doesn't help us if consent never comes.
- **This must be a genuine Condition Precedent to Completion:** receipt of an **unconditional written Bluefen consent (with conditions in 11.3 satisfied)** before we are obliged to complete. Upgrade "reasonable" to **"best endeavours."**
- If the Seller resists a hard CP, we need a **price adjustment / specific indemnity** for loss of Bluefen, and/or a **retention/escrow** tied to Bluefen continuing post-Completion.
- Given 30% revenue concentration, consider an earn-out or deferred consideration keyed to Bluefen retention.

## D. Riverlark facility and security (Cl 2/7; Disclosure §3) — debt-free/cash-free breach

Baseline is **debt-free/cash-free**. There is **~AUD 3.2m outstanding** with its own change-of-control (8.1) and discharge mechanics (9.2), and the Disclosure confirms it is **not repaid and no discharge of security is included.**

- The Seller proposes "**a release to be provided following Completion.**" **Unacceptable.** We will not complete with undischarged security over the target (and a possible change-of-control default triggered by the sale itself).
- Require, **at or before Completion**, a **payoff letter and deed of release/discharge of security** as a **CP and completion deliverable**, with debt repaid out of the funds flow (consistent with debt-free/cash-free — the AUD 3.2m should reduce proceeds to the Seller, not be left for us).
- Confirm the sale does not itself breach Riverlark's change-of-control clause before Completion.

## E. Funds flow and DD-005 closing bonuses (Disclosure §5) — AUD 420,000 leakage

The Seller says the **AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses "are a matter for the Seller"** and are **not itemised in the funds flow** — yet the Disclosure confirms these bonuses are **triggered by Completion** and are **continued-employment conditioned**, and that the funds flow omits them.

- These are **liabilities triggered by the transaction** and are likely **the Company's (our) liabilities** after Completion unless expressly allocated to the Seller. Saying it's "a matter for the Seller" without a contractual mechanism means **we** may bear them.
- Require a **specific indemnity** from the Seller for the AUD 420,000 **plus employer on-costs** (payroll tax, superannuation, SGC) — the Disclosure expressly notes it is silent on whether on-costs apply, so the real number is higher.
- Alternatively, treat as a **pre-Completion liability deducted in the funds flow** (price adjustment). Do **not** accept it being left off the funds flow with no allocation.

## F. Ironquay IP / SOW3 (Cl 11.1; Disclosure §4) — IP ownership risk

Under DD-004 cl 7.3, **transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.** DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 open**, and there is **no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment** in the data room.

- This means the Company **may not own key SOW3 IP** until payment clears and assignment is executed. The Seller's existing indemnity is **limited to the SOW3 payment itself** — which does **not** cover the real risk (loss of/clouded title to the IP, or the cost of re-procuring rights).
- **Push for:** (i) evidence of payment and executed assignment as a **completion deliverable**, or (ii) a **broad IP indemnity** covering loss arising from defective ownership/transfer of the SOW3 materials, not just the AUD 180k fee; plus a **specific IP ownership warranty** that the Company owns or validly licenses all IP used in the business.

## G. Export/privacy incident DD-006 (Cl 4.6/Schedule 6; Disclosure §6) — potential Privacy Act / NDB exposure

A **download link went to an unintended external address**; the export may contain **~1,240 records** (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material" and declines to characterise it as a breach.

- Under the **Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme**, if there is unauthorised access/disclosure of personal information likely to result in serious harm, **notification to the OAIC and affected individuals may be mandatory**. "We can't yet establish access/scope" is not comfort — it's unresolved risk, and the 2022 penalty increases make this potentially significant.
- The Seller's downplaying ("not expected to be material," "no loss amount") is a reason for *more* protection, not less.
- **Push for:** a **specific, uncapped (or separately capped, longer-surviving) indemnity** covering regulatory penalties, notification/remediation costs, third-party claims and investigation costs arising from DD-006; a **data-protection/compliance warranty**; and ideally **completion of the investigation (and any required notification) as a CP** or a tailored escrow pending resolution.

## H. Supplier renewals — three Sandbar renewals (Disclosure §8; §/DD-008/DD-011) — AUD 330,000

Three **related** renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330k aggregate). The Seller characterises them as "ordinary-course operating costs," but the **Disclosure itself says it does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.** Note the structuring: splitting into 3 × AUD 110k keeps each below likely materiality/consent thresholds, but **"read together"** they aggregate to AUD 330k.

- **Push back on the ordinary-course characterisation.** Require disclosure of terms (term length, termination rights, auto-renewal, total commitment). If these are **non-terminable multi-year commitments** entered pre-Completion, they should be dealt with as **assumed liabilities/price adjustment** or warranted, and the **anti-aggregation structuring** should be addressed in the conduct-of-business / leakage provisions.
- Ensure the **ordinary-course-of-business warranty and interim covenant** capture related-party / bundled commitments on an aggregated basis.

## I. Office lease notification (Disclosure §7) & J. Mossvale assignment restriction (Disclosure §9)

- **Lease (DD-007):** there is a **notification obligation**; Seller says it's not a landlord-consent requirement for a share sale. Likely correct that a pure share sale doesn't usually trip an assignment clause, but **verify the lease wording** for change-of-control provisions and confirm the notification is given — a **low-cost CP/covenant** to notify.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** restriction on assignment; Seller says consent not required "merely because shares are sold." Again, **verify** — check whether the contract has a **change-of-control** trigger distinct from assignment. Add a warranty that no material contract is terminable/breached by reason of the transaction (a **change-of-control warranty**), which forces the Seller to stand behind these characterisations.

## K. Title evidence (Disclosure §10; Cl Title) — DD-012 share register only

Title to 100% of shares is "**evidenced by the Company's own share register**," and the Disclosure expressly notes the **Buyer has not completed its own verification.**

- A company's own register is **not conclusive proof** of unencumbered beneficial ownership (it won't reveal, e.g., security interests, trusts, options, or prior transfers). Combined with the Seller's attempt to cap/time-limit title (points 3–4), this is a real gap.
- **We should:** conduct our own verification (**PPSR search** against the shares/Seller, ASIC searches, review of the constitution for pre-emption rights, and confirmation there are no options/convertibles); obtain a **full, uncapped title/capacity warranty**; and require delivery at Completion of **executed share transfers, original/updated register, share certificates (or evidence), and board approvals**.

## Summary of Recommendations

**Deal-structure / Conditions Precedent (hardest points):**
1. **Bluefen:** unconditional written consent (conditions in 11.3 met) as a **hard CP**; upgrade to **best endeavours**; fallback = price adjustment/indemnity/retention given 30% revenue concentration.
2. **Riverlark:** repayment from funds flow + **deed of release/discharge of security at Completion** as CP; preserve debt-free/cash-free (AUD 3.2m reduces Seller proceeds).
3. **DD-005 bonuses:** either deduct AUD 420k **plus on-costs** in the funds flow, or a **specific Seller indemnity** — do not leave unallocated.

**Liability architecture:**
4. **Reverse the "all Claims" default** — limitations apply only to general warranties unless expressly extended.
5. **Title/capacity:** uncapped (100%), 6–7 yr / no limit; back with our own PPSR/ASIC verification.
6. **Tax:** separate tax deed surviving ~7 yrs.
7. General cap: push **25–30%**; general time limit to **24 months**; confirm **tipping basket** not excess-only.

**Disclosure / knowledge:**
8. **Delete constructive/"discoverable" knowledge** (Cl 8.3); limit to actual knowledge of named individuals, ideally delete.
9. **Reject general data-room disclosure**; require **fair and specific** disclosure against each warranty.

**Specific indemnities / warranties (carve-outs from the cap, longer survival):**
10. **DD-006 privacy incident:** dedicated indemnity (penalties, notification, remediation, third-party claims) + data-protection warranty; consider CP/escrow.
11. **Ironquay SOW3 IP:** evidence of payment + executed assignment at Completion, or **broad IP-ownership indemnity** (not limited to the AUD 180k fee) + IP ownership warranty.
12. **Sandbar renewals:** disclose terms; treat aggregated AUD 330k properly; strengthen ordinary-course warranty + interim covenant (anti-aggregation/related-party bundling).
13. **Change-of-control warranty** covering lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) — force the Seller to stand behind its "no consent needed" characterisations; give lease notice.

**Diligence actions on our side:**
14. Independent title verification (PPSR, ASIC, constitution/pre-emption, options/convertibles) — do not rely on DD-012 alone.
15. Verify Riverlark and Bluefen change-of-control clauses are not tripped by signing/pre-Completion.

**Overall theme:** The Seller's package systematically (a) collapses all claims into one low cap and short time bar, (b) uses sweeping general disclosure + constructive-knowledge to neutralise the warranties, and (c) defers the two biggest execution risks (Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge) to *after* Completion while quietly leaving AUD 420k of bonuses and AUD 330k of renewals as our problem. Our mark-up should restore proper carve-outs, convert the two big risks into CPs, and pin specific indemnities on the four disclosed problem areas (Bluefen, Ironquay IP, the privacy incident, and the bonuses).

Happy to turn any of these into actual drafting / a mark-up of specific clauses — just point me at the clause wording you want redrafted.

Note: this is deal-support analysis, not a formal legal opinion; please have the responsible admitted practitioner settle the final positions.

## G. Export/privacy incident DD-006 (Cl 4.6/Schedule 6; Disclosure §6) — potential Privacy Act / NDB exposure

A **download link went to an unintended external address**; the export may contain **~1,240 records** (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material" and declines to characterise it as a breach.

- Under the **Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme**, if there is unauthorised access/disclosure of personal information likely to result in serious harm, **notification to the OAIC and affected individuals may be mandatory**. "We can't yet establish access/scope" is not comfort — it's unresolved risk, and the 2022 penalty increases make this potentially significant.
- The Seller's downplaying ("not expected to be material," "no loss amount") is a reason for *more* protection, not less.
- **Push for:** a **specific, uncapped (or separately capped, longer-surviving) indemnity** covering regulatory penalties, notification/remediation costs, third-party claims and investigation costs arising from DD-006; a **data-protection/compliance warranty**; and ideally **completion of the investigation (and any required notification) as a CP** or a tailored escrow pending resolution.

## H. Supplier renewals — three Sandbar renewals (Disclosure §8; §/DD-008/DD-011) — AUD 330,000

Three **related** renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330k aggregate). The Seller characterises them as "ordinary-course operating costs," but the **Disclosure itself says it does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.** Note the structuring: splitting into 3 × AUD 110k keeps each below likely materiality/consent thresholds, but **"read together"** they aggregate to AUD 330k.

- **Push back on the ordinary-course characterisation.** Require disclosure of terms (term length, termination rights, auto-renewal, total commitment). If these are **non-terminable multi-year commitments** entered pre-Completion, they should be dealt with as **assumed liabilities/price adjustment** or warranted, and the **anti-aggregation structuring** should be addressed in the conduct-of-business / leakage provisions.
- Ensure the **ordinary-course-of-business warranty and interim covenant** capture related-party / bundled commitments on an aggregated basis.

## I. Office lease notification (Disclosure §7) & J. Mossvale assignment restriction (Disclosure §9)

- **Lease (DD-007):** there is a **notification obligation**; Seller says it's not a landlord-consent requirement for a share sale. Likely correct that a pure share sale doesn't usually trip an assignment clause, but **verify the lease wording** for change-of-control provisions and confirm the notification is given — a **low-cost CP/covenant** to notify.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** restriction on assignment; Seller says consent not required "merely because shares are sold." Again, **verify** — check whether the contract has a **change-of-control** trigger distinct from assignment. Add a warranty that no material contract is terminable/breached by reason of the transaction (a **change-of-control warranty**), which forces the Seller to stand behind these characterisations.

## K. Title evidence (Disclosure §10; Cl Title) — DD-012 share register only

Title to 100% of shares is "**evidenced by the Company's own share register**," and the Disclosure expressly notes the **Buyer has not completed its own verification.**

- A company's own register is **not conclusive proof** of unencumbered beneficial ownership (it won't reveal, e.g., security interests, trusts, options, or prior transfers). Combined with the Seller's attempt to cap/time-limit title (points 3–4), this is a real gap.
- **We should:** conduct our own verification (**PPSR search** against the shares/Seller, ASIC searches, review of the constitution for pre-emption rights, and confirmation there are no options/convertibles); obtain a **full, uncapped title/capacity warranty**; and require delivery at Completion of **executed share transfers, original/updated register, share certificates (or evidence), and board approvals**.

## Summary of Recommendations

**Deal-structure / Conditions Precedent (hardest points):**
1. **Bluefen:** unconditional written consent (conditions in 11.3 met) as a **hard CP**; upgrade to **best endeavours**; fallback = price adjustment/indemnity/retention given 30% revenue concentration.
2. **Riverlark:** repayment from funds flow + **deed of release/discharge of security at Completion** as CP; preserve debt-free/cash-free (AUD 3.2m reduces Seller proceeds).
3. **DD-005 bonuses:** either deduct AUD 420k **plus on-costs** in the funds flow, or a **specific Seller indemnity** — do not leave unallocated.

**Liability architecture:**
4. **Reverse the "all Claims" default** — limitations apply only to general warranties unless expressly extended.
5. **Title/capacity:** uncapped (100%), 6–7 yr / no limit; back with our own PPSR/ASIC verification.
6. **Tax:** separate tax deed surviving ~7 yrs.
7. General cap: push **25–30%**; general time limit to **24 months**; confirm **tipping basket** not excess-only.

**Disclosure / knowledge:**
8. **Delete constructive/"discoverable" knowledge** (Cl 8.3); limit to actual knowledge of named individuals, ideally delete.
9. **Reject general data-room disclosure**; require **fair and specific** disclosure against each warranty.

**Specific indemnities / warranties (carve-outs from the cap, longer survival):**
10. **DD-006 privacy incident:** dedicated indemnity (penalties, notification, remediation, third-party claims) + data-protection warranty; consider CP/escrow.
11. **Ironquay SOW3 IP:** evidence of payment + executed assignment at Completion, or **broad IP-ownership indemnity** (not limited to the AUD 180k fee) + IP ownership warranty.
12. **Sandbar renewals:** disclose terms; treat aggregated AUD 330k properly; strengthen ordinary-course warranty + interim covenant (anti-aggregation/related-party bundling).
13. **Change-of-control warranty** covering lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) — force the Seller to stand behind its "no consent needed" characterisations; give lease notice.

**Diligence actions on our side:**
14. Independent title verification (PPSR, ASIC, constitution/pre-emption, options/convertibles) — do not rely on DD-012 alone.
15. Verify Riverlark and Bluefen change-of-control clauses are not tripped by signing/pre-Completion.

**Overall theme:** The Seller's package systematically (a) collapses all claims into one low cap and short time bar, (b) uses sweeping general disclosure + constructive-knowledge to neutralise the warranties, and (c) defers the two biggest execution risks (Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge) to *after* Completion while quietly leaving AUD 420k of bonuses and AUD 330k of renewals as our problem. Our mark-up should restore proper carve-outs, convert the two big risks into CPs, and pin specific indemnities on the four disclosed problem areas (Bluefen, Ironquay IP, the privacy incident, and the bonuses).
